task.description:
Hard gate on ADHOC-20260821-002's amendment of the pipeline's own rules — commit b13a523, 209 insertions and 0 deletions across six instruction/workflow files. Review `git show b13a523`.

This gate matters more than a normal one and the reason is worth stating: these five rules will be read by every future agent on this project, including weak models that will follow them literally, and there is no human reviewing runs afterwards. A rule that is wrong, ambiguous, or that contradicts a rule elsewhere in the doc set does not fail once — it fails quietly on every run until someone notices. Your role file's 'decision-record consistency' scope is the closest existing analogue; apply that standard to the instruction corpus as a whole.

The five rules, and the evidence each is supposed to carry, are specified in step-01-workflow-rules.json's task.description (R1..R5). Read that as the spec, then check what actually shipped against it.

FIVE THINGS TO GATE ON:

  1. **Is each rule TRUE?** These were derived from one session's observations, largely ORCH's own. Check the reasoning, not just the presence of a paragraph. In particular R1's claim that count-matching attribution is unsound rests on three runs producing 13, 15 and 14 failures — satisfy yourself the conclusion follows, and that the rule it produces (structural attribution) is actually achievable by an agent with the tools available. A rule that cannot be followed is worse than none, because it trains agents to report compliance they did not achieve.

  2. **Does anything CONTRADICT an existing rule?** This is the highest-value check. R4 in particular sits adjacent to Instruction Precedence, which makes the handoff's task block the top authority — R4 carves out factual claims from that. Verify the carve-out is stated so it cannot be misread as licence to disregard instructions, and that the safety/gate non-overridability survives intact. Also check R1 against core-directives' Unblock-Everything (which tells agents to fix blocking failures) and against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's file-and-forward rule — those must still compose.

  3. **Is any rule stated as a bare imperative without its evidence?** AC8 of the producing handoff makes that a FAIL for the rule in question. The doc set's convention is that every hard rule names the incident that produced it, precisely so a future agent can tell WHEN it applies rather than applying it blindly. Check each of the five.

  4. **Rule ONE SPECIFIC QUESTION the producer raised rather than decided.** DOC-UPDATER flagged that `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` was not in its scope, and that this is where Step Final agents are actually standing when R2's push rule (push only your own commit; a non-fast-forward rejection may just mean the other session already pushed; do not force) becomes relevant. It judged a pointer from there worth a follow-up. Decide: is the rule discoverable where it is needed, or is GIT_MERGE.md a required home? If you rule it required, say so as a FAIL with the specific addition needed — ORCH will route the rework. Note the same question applies to R1 and the Step Final agents, who also run test commands.

  5. **Duplication versus discoverability.** The producer put each rule in one canonical home with cross-references, except R1, which additionally carries a compressed operative checklist in WF-02 Step 4. It flagged this as a deliberate tension between its AC1 (state it where the agent stands) and AC9 (no duplication). Rule on whether that shape is right, and whether the same treatment is needed anywhere else.

Do NOT rewrite the docs yourself — you gate, ORCH routes rework. A FAIL must name each specific gap and the change that would close it.
acceptance_criteria: Each of R1..R5 is given an individual verdict on correctness — is the rule true and is it followable with the tools an agent actually has — with your reasoning, not merely a presence check
The instruction corpus is checked for contradictions introduced by these five, with R4-vs-Instruction-Precedence and R1-vs-Unblock-Everything/ISSUE_QUEUE checked explicitly and by name
Each of R1..R5 is confirmed to carry the incident that produced it, or named as failing that requirement

An explicit ruling on whether docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md is a required home for R2's push rule (and whether R1 needs a home there too), with the specific addition named if you rule it required
An explicit ruling on the R1 duplication shape in WF-02 Step 4, and whether any other rule needs the same treatment
The commit is confirmed additive — no existing rule deleted or weakened. State the check you ran
PASS or FAIL stated. A FAIL names each gap and the change that closes it
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
FAIL on R3's enforceability and on a missing required home in GIT_MERGE.md. R1, R2, R4 and R5 PASS individually; R3 passes on substance but as shipped is optional-by-precedence and hazardous-if-followed. Nothing in the commit is wrong on the facts -- all five rules' evidence was re-derived from source, not accepted from the producing summary.

EVIDENCE RE-DERIVED (not inherited). R1's measurement is real: test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0106-20260821.yaml lines 342-344 record Run 1 seed 928451 = 1247/1260, 13 failed and Run 2 seed 613644 = 1245/1260, 15 failed on the same commit; test/reports/report-20260820-WF02-REQ066-20260820.yaml line 35 records 'Result: 1216/1230 passed' = 14 failures, with Letflow.Definitions.PromotionTest + PromotionAssertionRerunTest present there (line 168) and absent from both later runs. PinRebindTest exists (test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs) and the 513-517-whitespace vs. line-351 reasoning is recorded at report lines 354-361. R3's mutant counts are real: test/specs/ISS-0106.md lines 372-374 give 17/30, 24/30, 11/30, and handoffs/WF03-ISS0106-20260821/step-04b-test-design-validation.json records the validator applying mutants A and C itself and reproducing 17/30 and 11/30 exactly. R4's two worked examples are both recorded in that run's handoffs. R5's on-pin/off-pin probe is recorded. AC8 is MET for all five -- every rule names the incident that produced it.

ADDITIVE CHECK (AC6 of this gate). `git show b13a523 --numstat --format=''` returns 27/0, 74/0, 40/0, 27/0, 29/0, 12/0, 72/0 -- 281 insertions, ZERO deletions across all seven files. `git show b13a523 --format='' | grep -c '^-[^-]'` returns 0, so not one line of existing rule text was removed or reworded; every change is a new section or an appended paragraph. `git show b13a523 --name-only` lists exactly the six owned_modules files plus the step-01 handoff -- nothing outside scope. No existing rule is deleted or weakened, and none needed superseding.

PER-RULE VERDICTS.

R1 -- PASS (true, followable, evidenced). The inference holds: if one commit yields 13 then 15 ten minutes apart, set-identity with a prior run cannot establish pre-existence, and the symmetric claim (a delta proves regression) fails by the same measurement. TEST-RUNNER's 'simultaneously a regression AND a fix' consequence is not rhetoric, it follows directly. Both structural tests are executable with tools an agent has (`git diff --name-only main...HEAD`; a merge-base checkout and re-run). The in-the-diff subsection correctly makes mechanism rather than proximity the standard and refuses BOTH lazy readings.

R2 -- PASS (true, followable, evidenced). Both halves of the incident are named. The re-read-before-write rule is genuinely enforceable because the edit tooling already rejects a stale read -- which is how the incident surfaced. `git push origin <your-sha>:main` does what the text claims when your commit is the earlier one. The non-fast-forward-may-mean-already-pushed clause is the single most valuable sentence in R2, because the default reaction to that rejection is to force. AC4's 'removes the subagents from the race, not another ORCH-role session' is stated in both ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1 and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 4, correctly as statement-plus-pointer rather than duplication.

R3 -- FAIL (true and well-argued, but NOT followable as shipped; two gaps, both fixable additively). The reasoning is correct and important: UndefinedFunctionError against a missing module is a coarse control that cannot discriminate a correct implementation from a wrong one, and the three-mutant evidence proves the technique works. Two gaps make the rule unenforceable or unsafe -- see issues G1 and G2.

R4 -- PASS, and the carve-out is correctly bounded. This was the highest-risk item and it survives scrutiny. The core-directives paragraph is placed INSIDE the Instruction Precedence section, immediately after its two override rules, so an agent reading precedence cannot miss the carve-out. The do-versus-is-true line is drawn explicitly in both files. The safety/gate non-overridability not only survives, it is STRENGTHENED: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1 adds 'never overridable by anything, INCLUDING YOUR OWN MEASUREMENT', which closes the one abuse the carve-out would otherwise open ('I measured that this gate is unnecessary'). I probed the riskiest sentence, 'A verified disagreement outranks the handoff', for misreadability: read in isolation it could sound like measurement beats instruction, but it is scoped by the preceding clause to 'a checkable factual claim' and immediately followed by the not-licence paragraph. More importantly, the residual ambiguity does not change what an agent DOES -- the dotted/underscored example is itself a case where a false premise was embedded in something instruction-shaped, and the prescribed action (deviate, then report the deviation in result.issues, never comply silently and never diverge silently) is correct under either reading. An ambiguity that produces the same action either way is not a defect in a rule binding weak models. No contradiction with core-directives' 'Never resolve a conflict silently' -- 1.1 requires the same result.issues reporting.

R5 -- PASS (true, followable, evidenced). It closes a real hole in the producer/validator section: that section demanded re-derivation but not that the re-derivation be run under conditions where the property could fail. 'Construct them if the ambient environment does not supply them' is judgement-laden but anchored by a concrete worked example. The case where conditions cannot be constructed is already governed by core-directives' No Speculation ('if you cannot verify, say so explicitly'), so it composes rather than dangling. Disclosure: this rule's evidence was produced by this same role on WF03-ISS0106-20260821; I re-read the recorded probe rather than relying on that.

CONTRADICTION SWEEP (AC2 of this gate).

R4 vs Instruction Precedence -- checked by name. NO CONTRADICTION. The chain resolves conflicts between instruction SOURCES; 1.1 governs FACTUAL CLAIMS. Disjoint domains, and the new paragraph says so in terms. Non-overridability of safety/gate rules intact and strengthened.

R1 vs Unblock-Everything -- checked by name. NO CONTRADICTION; they compose, and R1 in fact SUPPLIES what Unblock-Everything was missing. That directive's 'Scope boundary' paragraph already splits blocking defects (fix now) from merely-noticed ones (file and forward) but never said how to tell which bucket a test failure is in; R1 is exactly that procedure. See MINOR issue G4 -- the two sections sit ~70 lines apart in the same file with no cross-reference.

R1 vs ISSUE_QUEUE.md file-and-forward -- checked by name. COMPOSES, with one MINOR drift, G5. ISSUE_QUEUE's Purpose paragraph draws the same incidental-vs-blocking line and R1 defers to it correctly in core-directives ('per ISSUE_QUEUE.md and No Issue Left Local-Only above'). But ISSUE_QUEUE was amended 2026-08-21 so ids are allocated atomically by letflow-queue and 'the discovering agent reports the finding, it does not call gh or the queue itself'. WF-02 Step 4's checklist item 3 says a uncovered failure 'is called out AS SUCH and filed' without the deferring parenthetical the core-directives version carries -- read literally by TEST-RUNNER that instructs an agent to do what ISSUE_QUEUE forbids it to do.

R3 vs .claude/agents/test-design-validator.md -- NOT in the sweep I was asked for, and the most serious finding in this gate. See G1: it is a PRECEDENCE-INVERTED contradiction.

R2 vs GIT_MERGE.md -- no contradiction (GIT_MERGE never pushes to main directly; it pushes feature/<run-id> and merges by PR, so R2's push rule addresses a different path, the ORCH direct-to-main docs-only path). But see G3.

RULING 1 (this gate's AC4) -- IS GIT_MERGE.md A REQUIRED HOME? YES, REQUIRED -- and the load-bearing need is R1, not R2. DOC-UPDATER asked the right question and understated it. See G3 for the specific additions. This is legitimately rework rather than a producer miss: GIT_MERGE.md was not in step-01's owned_modules, so DOC-UPDATER could not have written it. ORCH must widen owned_modules on the rework handoff.

RULING 2 (this gate's AC5) -- THE R1 DUPLICATION SHAPE IS RIGHT; the WF-02 Step 4 checklist is short enough and should stay. AC1 and AC9 are not actually in conflict once 'duplication' is read as duplication of the EVIDENCE NARRATIVE rather than of the operative test. The checklist carries four operative points and a single parenthetical clause for the measurement; the 13/14/15 story, the three-run comparison and the PinRebindTest mechanism all live only in core-directives. That is the correct split, and it is the split core-directives' own weak-model-tolerance clause demands: 'every role file, workflow doc, and guide must be explicit and mechanical enough that an agent with limited judgement still produces correct work by following the steps literally' -- an agent standing in WF-02 Step 4 must not have to follow a pointer to learn the test. No other rule needs the checklist treatment: R2 has one audience and one home, R3 is already stated in-place where its agent stands, R4's operative sentence is in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL where every agent claims its handoff, R5 is a short addition in the section it modifies. The real inconsistency is one of FORM, not volume -- see MINOR issue G6: WF-04's version is prose of comparable length to WF-02's checklist but less scannable and less mechanically executable. If rework touches WF-04, give it the same four-point form.

SCOPE OF THIS STEP. No file outside handoffs/ was modified by me. `git status --porcelain` before commit shows only this handoff file as my change; docs/ and lib/ untouched. I did not write handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH's). completed_at read from the clock via `date -u`, not from memory.

issues.description: G1 -- R3 IS OVERRIDDEN BY A HIGHER-PRECEDENCE FILE AND IS THEREFORE OPTIONAL AS SHIPPED. WF-03 (Instruction Precedence rank 3) now states that TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR 'must independently APPLY at least one of the reported mutants and run it'. But `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` (rank 2, HIGHER) says of the WF-03 regression case only: 'confirm the spec states (and, IF YOU CAN VERIFY IT YOURSELF CHEAPLY, confirms) that the test actually failed against the pre-fix code.' A literal-minded validator applying the precedence chain correctly concludes the mutant run is discretionary and gated on a cheapness test. This is the worst shape of contradiction for a weak-model pipeline: the new mandatory rule sits BELOW the permissive text it exists to tighten, so following the rules correctly defeats the rule. CHANGE THAT CLOSES IT: amend `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md`'s 'What you do' section, WF-03 clause, to read that where the pre-fix failure is that the code under test did not exist, you MUST additionally apply at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutants to the shipped logic yourself, run the suite, and quote your own measured counts -- not subject to a cheapness test and not satisfiable by reading the reported counts -- citing WF-03's 'When the pre-fix failure is the code under test does not exist'. Note that `.claude/agents/` was not in step-01's owned_modules, so ORCH must widen owned_modules on the rework handoff.

G2 -- R3 TELLS A GATE AGENT TO MUTATE lib/ AND NEVER TELLS IT TO REVERT. WF-03's new subsection instructs TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to apply a mutant to the shipped logic and run it, but says nothing about isolating or reverting the mutation. A gate step is normally bound by 'no file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step', so as written the rule instructs an agent to violate its own scope constraint, and a weak model can leave a deliberately-broken module in lib/ on the branch. The run this rule is drawn from did NOT have this hazard because its handoff carried an explicit AC ('any mutant you applied is reverted, with the revert verified and stated'), and the validator complied by reverting via `git checkout --`, re-checking the module SHA1 against pristine, confirming `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty, and re-running to 30 passed -- none of which survived into the general rule. CHANGE THAT CLOSES IT: append to the WF-03 subsection the technique the cited run actually used -- apply mutants in a throwaway `git worktree` of the branch, or, if applied in place, revert with `git checkout -- <path>` and VERIFY the revert before completing the handoff by confirming `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` is empty and the test file re-runs green, quoting both. State that leaving a mutant in the tree is a step failure.

G3 -- GIT_MERGE.md IS A REQUIRED HOME, PRIMARILY FOR R1 (this gate's ruling on the question DOC-UPDATER raised). DOC-UPDATER framed this as a discoverability nicety for R2's push rule; it is more than that, and the stronger case is R1. GIT_MERGE.md is read by ELIXIR-DEV and FRONTEND-DEV and is where Step Final agents stand, and it makes them run the full suite in TWO places with no attribution rule and no pointer to one: (i) the Precondition section makes the pre-merge gate 'mix format --check-formatted && mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test ... has been run and REPORTED GREEN in this run's own handoffs'; (ii) step 5d (post-conflict verification) says 'mix test / If FAIL: complete-handoff(status: FAIL, issues: [{severity: BLOCKER, description: build/tests failed after rebase}]), ORCH routes to ISSUE-FIXER'. This suite has a standing 13-15 pre-existing failures and has had for days -- so BOTH instructions are unsatisfiable as literally written, and the only way agents have been reconciling them is the count-matching that R1 now forbids. Leaving GIT_MERGE.md silent means R1 is unreachable at exactly the step where a wrong attribution merges to main. REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) at step 5d, after `mix test`, add: 'This suite carries a standing set of pre-existing failures. Before reporting FAIL, attribute EACH failure per core-directives.md''s Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching -- only a failure you can attribute to this branch is a BLOCKER here; one you have structurally cleared is filed and forwarded per ISSUE_QUEUE.md and does not block this step. Do not attribute by comparing counts with a previous run.' (b) in the Precondition section, qualify 'reported green' the same way, with the same pointer. (c) SECONDARY, for R2: one line under step 2 or step 6 -- 'If another ORCH-role session is live in this same checkout, `git status` at step 2 may show its files and `git log` its commits: stage by filename only (already required above) and push only your own SHA; see ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1.' Step 2 already forbids `git add -A` for precisely this shared-checkout reason, so this is a natural amendment rather than a new section. R2's `git push origin <your-sha>:main` rule itself does NOT need restating here, because GIT_MERGE's flow never pushes to main directly -- it pushes feature/<run-id> and merges by PR -- and restating it risks an agent misapplying a direct-to-main push inside the PR flow. Pointer only.

G4 -- R1 and Unblock-Everything do not cross-reference each other despite sitting ~70 lines apart in core-directives.md and being two halves of one decision. Unblock-Everything's 'Scope boundary' paragraph draws the blocking-vs-noticed line but has never said how to decide which side a test failure falls on; R1 is now that procedure. Suggested addition (one clause, no duplication): in Unblock-Everything's Scope boundary paragraph, after 'A defect you merely notice while working', add 'for a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching below, not by judgement'.

G5 -- WF-02 Step 4's checklist item 3 instructs TEST-RUNNER that an uncovered failure 'is called out AS SUCH and filed', dropping the deferring parenthetical that the core-directives version carries ('per ISSUE_QUEUE.md and No Issue Left Local-Only above'). ISSUE_QUEUE.md was amended 2026-08-21 (ADHOC-20260821-001) so that issue ids are allocated atomically by letflow-queue and 'only ORCH calls the queue -- the discovering agent REPORTS the finding, it does not call gh or the queue itself'. As written, WF-02's item 3 tells TEST-RUNNER to do what ISSUE_QUEUE forbids it to do, and the id-collision class that amendment exists to prevent is exactly what a discovering agent filing directly reproduces. CHANGE: item 3 to read '... is called out AS SUCH and reported for filing per ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- never folded into the known set.'

G6 -- form inconsistency between R1's two operative statements. WF-02 Step 4 got a four-point fenced checklist; WF-04 Step 1 got a prose paragraph of comparable length carrying the same four points in a single run-on sentence. The WF-02 shape is correct and should be the model (see this gate's Ruling 2). If rework touches WF-04, give its paragraph the same four-point form -- same content, materially easier for a weak model to execute and to report against point by point. Non-gating.

G7 -- R1's two structural tests are stated as exhaustive ('you must show ONE OF THESE TWO THINGS') but the very run they are drawn from cleared its failures by a THIRD form of argument: a demonstrated non-branch MECHANISM (stray erl.exe processes from an earlier nested suite holding 65 connections to letflow_test, making the environmental failure set vary run to run). That class is also the one where the merge-base test is least reliable, since a nondeterministic environmental failure may simply not reproduce in one merge-base run. Read literally, an agent facing this suite's dominant failure class can satisfy neither named test, and the predictable weak-model response is to assert the git-diff test loosely -- i.e. false compliance, the exact failure mode this gate's brief warns about. The rule is SAFE as written because its third bullet routes anything unattributed to filing, so erring costs an issue record rather than a missed regression; that is why this is MINOR and not gating. SUGGESTED ADDITION: a third permitted form -- 'a demonstrated mechanism outside this branch, stated causally and with its evidence (the stray-process contention in WF03-ISS0106-20260821 is the worked example)' -- plus one explicit sentence: 'If you can show none of these, you may not call the failure pre-existing. Report it as unattributed and file it.'

result.next_action: ORCH routes rework to DOC-UPDATER for G1, G2 and G3, widening owned_modules to include `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` (G1) and `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` (G3) -- neither was in step-01's owned_modules, so this is scope that DOC-UPDATER could not have covered, not a producer miss. G4-G7 are MINOR and may be folded into the same rework turn or deferred; none blocks. R1, R2, R4 and R5 need no change and the existing commit b13a523 should NOT be reverted -- rework is additive on top of it. Re-gate at REVIEWER after rework (rework_count 1 of 3).
